name: fft
description: A synthesizable, parameterizable streaming Fast Fourier Transform accelerator.
authorship: Zero ASIC Corporation; author Andreas Olofsson

human_review.notes: Provenance (model and date) confirmed by the author; architecture, scope, and verification were directed and reviewed by the author.

spec.summary: Synthesizable, parameterizable streaming FFT accelerator using a radix-2 decimation-in-frequency single-path delay feedback (R2SDF) pipeline. It accepts one complex sample per clock and, after the pipeline fills, produces one complex frequency bin per clock; total latency is ~N + LOG2N cycles. The design has LOG2N = log2(N) pipeline stages, each a radix-2 butterfly plus a feedback delay line of depth N/2^(stage+1) plus a complex twiddle multiplier fed by a shared sine ROM. Data is Q1.15 signed fixed-point (DW=16), with each stage scaling its butterfly outputs by 1/2 so the result is the true FFT divided by N (block scaling that keeps Q1.15 from overflowing). Output is in native R2SDF bit-reversed bin order. The twiddle source is a 256-entry sine ROM read combinationally, so it folds into LUTs (not BRAM) and the twiddle multiplies map to DSP blocks.
key_decisions: Radix-2 DIF single-path delay feedback (R2SDF) pipeline with one complex sample in/out per clock and LOG2N stages.
Per-stage 1/2 butterfly scaling so the output is the FFT divided by N, keeping Q1.15 fixed-point from overflowing.
Twiddle source is a 256-entry sine ROM emitted as a synthesizable combinational case (sinrom), which maps to LUTs (zero BRAM) and survives --ignore-initial.
Output is left in native R2SDF bit-reversed order; bit-reversal reorder is intentionally omitted to keep the core small.
N is limited to <= 256 because the twiddle source is a 256-entry sine ROM.
rtl/fft.v is emitted by genfft.py, which generates the exact twiddle case table for the chosen ROM resolution.

origin.notes: Original implementation written for LogikBench; follows the cited algorithm/standard and hardware architectures, not copied from any specific HDL source.

references: J. W. Cooley and J. W. Tukey, 'An algorithm for the machine calculation of complex Fourier series,' Mathematics of Computation, vol. 19, no. 90, pp. 297-301, 1965.
E. H. Wold and A. M. Despain, 'Pipeline and parallel-pipeline FFT processors for VLSI implementations,' IEEE Trans. Computers, vol. C-33, no. 5, pp. 414-426, May 1984.
S. He and M. Torkelson, 'A new approach to pipeline FFT processor,' Proc. 10th Int. Parallel Processing Symp. (IPPS), pp. 766-770, 1996.
K. K. Parhi, VLSI Digital Signal Processing Systems, Wiley, 1999 -- chapter on FFT architectures (pipelined SDF, scaling, twiddle ROMs).
